reason: Both make the headline clear: the prefix gate let 5 of 14 forbidden requests through, the scoped gate 0 of 14 with 8 of 8 jobs done, and read-only blocked 4 of 8. A is a compact animated diagram in one fixed card that would make a good GIF, and its tap-a-card steps (3 and 5) draw each trick's real route on the map. B teaches non-engineers better: it explains the rules and paths as addresses (2/7), asks for a prediction before each reveal (3/7, 4/7), walks each path one folder at a time, and its 'Try both gates' tester (5/7) resolves paths the reader edits correctly. B is also more careful on 7/7: it says the other 9 forbidden requests were stopped only because they started outside the folder or asked for a command, that the scoped gate's perfect score is by design, and what was not tested. A's step 6 wrongly says only the prefix gate let forbidden requests in (observe-only let in all 14), and its diagram text is very small at phone width.

A: Step 6 text says 'Only the prefix gate let forbidden ones in', but observe-only let all 14 in; it also never explains that the other 9 forbidden requests were blocked only because they started outside the folder or asked for a command
Diagram labels, request paths and handwritten card labels are about 10-11 px at 390 px width and hard to read; the 'Agent asks to delete' and 'fooled so far' lines sit cramped side by side
The step-dot navigation wraps, so the 7th dot sits alone on a second row under the other six
B: Many steps (2/7, 4/7, 5/7, 6/7) run longer than the phone screen, so the walk animation and verdicts scroll under the sticky Back/Next bar; long monospace paths break mid-word; the long scrolling layout is harder to turn into a GIF
On 4/7 the row of trick chips scrolls sideways and is clipped ('e shortcut', '5. Secret i'); on 6/7 the popup from tapping a square covers the gate rows below it
The 'STEP n' labels are one behind the page counter (page 2/7 is 'STEP 1'), and the untrusted_approval popup mentions an 'approval claim in document' although the request carries no forged approval
